title: Security & Approvals
allowlist: Tool Allowlist (read-only default; high-risk needs human approval)
llmUntrusted: LLM output is always untrusted and must never execute directly
totpWhy1: Stolen passwords alone cannot sign in without the app code
totpWhy2: Sensitive actions can re-prompt for TOTP (step-up)
totpWhy3: Works with Google Authenticator, Authy, NordPass, 1Password, and more
totpAppsHint: Suggested apps: Google Authenticator, Authy, Microsoft Authenticator, NordPass, 1Password
totpScanHint: Open your authenticator app → Add account → Scan this QR.
totpManualHint: If you cannot scan, choose manual entry in the app and paste this Base32 secret.
totpQrFailed: Could not render QR — use the secret key below
totpResetHint: Reset issues a new QR/secret (old app entries stop working)
reauthPasswordHint: Start/reset 2FA requires password again (stolen session protection)
totpSecretGenerated: Secret ready — scan the QR or copy the key, then enter the app’s 6-digit code
confirmCodeHint: After scanning, enter the 6 digits currently shown in your authenticator.
totpEnabledSaveCodes: 2FA enabled — save the recovery codes below now (shown once)
recoveryCodesHint: Recovery codes are shown once only
webauthnUnsupported: This page has no WebAuthn API. In Brave/Chrome/Firefox avoid restricted modes; use a password manager if needed, and open the panel on a domain over HTTPS.
webauthnInsecureContext: This page is not a secure context ({{origin}}). Browsers require HTTPS or localhost for Passkeys — unrelated to Brave/NordPass. Open https://your-domain instead.
webauthnIpHost: You opened the panel via IP ({{origin}}). WebAuthn forbids IP as RP ID, so Brave/NordPass will fail. Bind a domain + HTTPS (e.g. https://panel.example.com) and retry.
webauthnCancelled: Cancelled or timed out. Try again.
passkeyHint: For high-risk step-up; needs HTTPS + domain.
apiKeysEmptyHint: Create from the toolbar; then call API with Bearer token
allowlistEmpty: No agent tools in the catalog
createApiKeyDesc: Full token is shown only once after create
apiKeyNameHint: Easy to recognize, e.g. CI / backup script
apiKey2faHint: If 2FA is on, creating a key requires a verification code (step-up).
backupCopied: Encrypted backup copied to clipboard (store offline)

ssh.jobOutboundDesc: Create outbound identity keys · panel peer / project git
ssh.jobLoginDesc: Register public keys to project home · authorized_keys
ssh.purposePanelHint: Cluster peer, backup scp, remote probes
ssh.purposeUserHint: Project Linux user git / scp / scripts
ssh.loginEmptyHint: Paste a laptop or CI public key, bind to a project user for SFTP/SSH (needs sshd snippet)
ssh.loginModalDesc: After selecting a project, the key is written to that Linux user home/
ssh.publicKeyHint: Paste full line, e.g. ssh-ed25519 AAAA… comment
ssh.loginNeedProject: Create a project first. Binding works best when the system user is ready.
ssh.loginNeedPub: Select a project or Linux user, and paste a public key starting with ssh-
ssh.loginNoProjects: No projects. Authorize an existing Linux user (root / tester) below. Writing /root/.ssh needs YSK_EXECUTE=1.
ssh.loginLinuxHint: Used when no project. Example: root or tester.
ssh.sshdDesc: Let ysks_* / ysk_* project users SFTP with public keys
ssh.sshdStep1: Add public keys under Login auth for projects
ssh.sshdStep2: Preview and install system Match snippets here
ssh.sshdStep3: Install needs system execute rights; will try to reload sshd
ssh.sshdManualHint: If execute is blocked, run the control plane with privileges, or place the snippet under
ssh.outboundDesc: Private keys encrypted in control plane
ssh.outboundEmptyHint: Create a key in ~30s: pick purpose → name → done. Use for peer / backup / git.
ssh.outboundEmptyFilterHint: Try changing filters or clear search
ssh.cannotWriteNeedExecute: Cannot write to system: enable execute (YSK_EXECUTE)
ssh.copiedPubPaste: Public key copied — paste into peer authorized_keys or Git deploy key
ssh.rotated: Rotated: old key retired, new key created
ssh.suggestFlow: Suggested: store → write disk → put public key on peer → test connection
ssh.allowLocalLogin: Allow local login with this key
ssh.localLoginOk: Public key added to local login authorization
ssh.wizStepPurposeDesc: Pick purpose so list and install path align
ssh.wizStepProjectDesc: Key binds to that project's Linux user and home
ssh.wizStepPanelDesc: Private key stays in control-plane secrets for scp/ssh to other hosts
ssh.wizStepNameDesc: Name for recognition; advanced options can wait
ssh.noProjectsHint: No projects yet — create a project and system user first
ssh.privKeyStayLocal: Private key stays on this control plane; never in lists or logs.
ssh.installImmediately: Write to disk immediately after create
ssh.installImmediatelyHint: (needs system execute; otherwise you will be told it cannot apply)
ssh.savePrivDesc: After close, full private key will not be shown again
ssh.privSavedConfirm: I stored the private key safely (password manager / offline backup)
ssh.testConnDesc: Try ssh … true with this identity. Success only means this target is reachable.
ssh.deleteIdentityDesc: Delete "{{name}}" and try to remove the private key file on disk
ssh.rotateKeyDesc: "{{name}}" will be retired and a new key created. Update peer authorized_keys.
ssh.needProjectOrUser: Select a project or enter a Linux username
ssh.totpGenerated: SSH-only TOTP generated (separate from panel 2FA unless you sync)
ssh.ssh2faDesc: Protects ssh login for Linux users
ssh.ssh2faStep1: Enroll TOTP for a Linux user (scan QR)
ssh.ssh2faStep4: Install PAM module and merge snippets (below)
ssh.ssh2faEmpty: No Linux user has SSH 2FA yet
ssh.pamTitle: System: PAM / sshd (manual or apply when permitted)
ssh.pamDesc: nullok avoids locking users without files. File written ≠ TOTP required.
ssh.rescueUsers: Rescue users (comma-separated, never in strict Match)
ssh.pamRescueHint: . Keep at least one rescue admin without a 2FA file (default root).
ssh.enrollModalDesc: Default: independent secret (not shared with panel)
ssh.advancedSharePanel: Advanced: use current panel operator TOTP secret (type SHARED to confirm)
ssh.setupAuthDesc: Scan or enter secret, then confirm with App 6-digit code
ssh.scanThenCode: If already scanned, enter the current 6-digit code.
ssh.sharePanelDesc: High risk. Type SHARED to confirm.
ssh.invalidPub: Paste a full OpenSSH public key line (ssh-ed25519 / ssh-rsa / ecdsa…).
ssh.dryRunOk: Dry-run finished. Review the preview below.
ssh.strictBlocked: Package or PAM is not ready; Strict apply is disabled.
ssh.privCloseWithoutAck: Closed. The private key will not be shown again; generate a new one if you did not save it.

noSessionsHint: When you sign in again, this device will appear here.
revokeSessionDesc: End session for {{device}} ({{ip}}). That device will need to sign in again.
revokeOthersDesc: This will end {{count}} other session(s). Your current browser stays signed in.
policyTotpHint: Site policy: each admin must enable their own 2FA (individual QR)
strictNeedsEnrolled: Enable 2FA on this admin account before turning on Strict.
policyTotpNeedSelf: Enable 2FA on this account first; the confirm code cannot be filled otherwise.
policyNoTotpHint: This account has no 2FA yet. Turn on 2FA above before requiring it for admins or all users — otherwise you can lock everyone out.
policyNeedSelf2fa: Enable 2FA on this account first, then confirm with a TOTP code
revokeAllDevicesTitle: Revoke every remembered device — you and other admins must verify 2FA again
strictConfirmDesc: Users without 2FA will be refused sign-in. Confirm you already have a working TOTP or passkey.
approvalsHint: Approvals appear when a high-risk tool needs a second operator. Grant approvals.review / approvals.handle on Users → Permissions.
allowlistReadonly: Read-only catalog of agent tools. Capability grants are configured on Users → Permissions.
confirmDeleteApiKeyDesc: “{{name}}” will stop authenticating. This cannot be undone.
